Lobbying the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)

Data

load(here("data/all_contacts.RData"))
# one obs per member per letter for all agencies
d <- all_contacts %>% 
  # define d as just FERC
  filter(agency=="DOE_FERC") %>% 
  select(-SUBJECT) %>% 
  mutate(majority = ifelse(majority == 1, "Majority", "Minority"))

# one obs per member per letter per committee for all agencies
load(here("data/all_contacts_committees.RData"))
# define dcommittees as just FERC
dcommittees <- all_contacts_committees %<>% filter(agency == "DOE_FERC")

# Coded letters, one obs per member per letter 
load(here("data/DOE_FERC-letters-coded.RData")) 
# TO DO: replace with DOE_FERC-letters-corps.Rdata when corps added
FERC_letters %<>% 
  select(ID, SUBJECT, 
         Freelancer, Cosigned_House, Cosigned_Senate,
         text_clean, Constituent, year,
         Place_State, Place_District, Place_District, 
         ProBusiness, AntiBusiness, ProProject, AntiProject) %>% 
  distinct()

# merge in coded letters
d %<>% left_join(FERC_letters) %>% filter(year <2019)

In all, we have 7600 letters received by FERC and marked “congressional” since 1990. Most, but not all of these are from Members of the U.S. Congress. For this paper, we focus on 4308 letters from 2000-2018.

Many letters are cosigned, yeilding 7093 members-level observations for years 2000-2018.

By party

d %>% 
  mutate(For = ifelse(tolower(Constituent) =="yes", "Constituent", NA),
         For = ifelse(!is.na(ProBusiness), "Business", For)) %>% 
  count(party, For, majority) %>% 
  filter(party != "(I)",
         !is.na(For),
         !is.na(majority)) %>% 
  ggplot() + 
  aes(y = n, x = party, fill = For) + 
  geom_col( position = "dodge") + 
  coord_flip() + facet_grid(. ~ majority) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "A")

Some letters oppose businesses:

d %>% 
  mutate(position = ifelse(!is.na(ProBusiness), "ProBusiness", NA),
         position = ifelse(!is.na(AntiBusiness), "AntiBusiness", position)#,
         #position = ifelse(!is.na(AntiBusiness)&!is.na(ProBusiness), "Both", position),
         #position = ifelse(is.na(position)&!is.na(Constituent), "Neutral Constituent", position)
         ) %>% 
  count(party, position, majority) %>% 
  filter(party != "(I)",
         !is.na(position),
         !is.na(majority)) %>% 
  ggplot() + 
  aes(y = n, x = party, fill = position) + 
  geom_col( position = "dodge") + 
  coord_flip() + facet_grid(. ~ majority)+ 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "C")

Coding of constituent type

Our coding of letter type is a mix of hand coding “Pro-business” and “Constituent” letters, as well as some coding rules applied to letters that were not put in either group by human coders (click CODE to see inductively-developed coding rules):

d %<>%
  mutate(TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", TYPE) & grepl("CONSTITUENT", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                        "1", TYPE)) %>%
  mutate(CERTAINTY = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", CERTAINTY) & grepl("CONSTITUENT", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                             "2", CERTAINTY)) %>%
  ## Corporate service?
  mutate(TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", TYPE) & grepl("ROCKIES EXPRESS PIPELINE|ELECTRIC GENERATOR PROJECT", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                        "2", TYPE)) %>%
  mutate(CERTAINTY = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", CERTAINTY) & grepl("ROCKIES EXPRESS PIPELINE|ELECTRIC GENERATOR PROJECT", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                             "3", CERTAINTY)) %>%
  ## or policy
  mutate(ALT_TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", ALT_TYPE) & grepl("ROCKIES EXPRESS PIPELINE|ELECTRIC GENERATOR PROJECT", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                            "5", ALT_TYPE)) %>%
  ## Policy work
  mutate(TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", TYPE) & grepl("COMMENTS OF US SENATOR|REQUEST INFORMATION|SENATOR.*COMMENTS|HEARING|MEETING|US SENATE SUBMITS|OVERSIGHT OF THE|EXPRESSING CONCERNS|SENATE SUBMITS COMMENTS", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                        "5", TYPE)) %>%
  mutate(CERTAINTY = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", CERTAINTY) & grepl("COMMENTS OF US SENATOR|REQUEST INFORMATION|SENATOR.*COMMENTS|HEARING|MEETING|US SENATE SUBMITS|OVERSIGHT OF THE|EXPRESSING CONCERNS|SENATE SUBMITS COMMENTS", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                             "1", CERTAINTY)) %>%
  ## Local government
  mutate(TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", TYPE) & grepl("CITY OF.*APPLICATION|APPLICATION.*CITY OF|ON BEHALF OF.*COUNTY", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                        "3", TYPE)) %>%
  mutate(CERTAINTY = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", CERTAINTY) & grepl("CITY OF.*APPLICATION|APPLICATION.*CITY OF|ON BEHALF OF.*COUNTY", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                             "1", CERTAINTY)) %>%
  ## Corporate service
  mutate(TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", TYPE) & grepl("NEW COAL", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                        "4", TYPE)) %>%
  mutate(CERTAINTY = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", CERTAINTY) & grepl("NEW COAL", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                             "2", CERTAINTY)) %>%
  mutate(ALT_TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", ALT_TYPE) & grepl("NEW COAL", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                            "5", ALT_TYPE)) %>%
  ## PUCs = nonprofits, right?
  mutate(TYPE = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", TYPE) & grepl("PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                        "3", TYPE)) %>%
  mutate(CERTAINTY = ifelse (!grepl("[0-9]", CERTAINTY) & grepl("PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION", SUBJECT, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                             "1", CERTAINTY))

FERC has an especially high ratio of letters written on behalf of businesses compared other agencies that mostly recieve letters from legislators on behalf of their constituents.

d %<>%  
  mutate(Type = as.character(Type)) %>% 
  mutate(Type = ifelse(tolower(Constituent) =="yes", "Indiv. Constituent", Type)) %>% 
  mutate(Type = ifelse(!is.na(ProBusiness), "Corp. Constituent", Type)) 

d %>% 
  filter(Type != "To be coded") %>%  
  mutate(total = n()) %>% 
  group_by(Type, total) %>% summarise(nT = n()) %>% 
  mutate(percent = paste0(nT, " = ", 100*round(nT/total, 2), "%")) %>% 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_col(aes(x = Type, y = nT)) + 
  geom_text(aes(x = Type, y = nT, label = percent), vjust = -.1) +
  labs(x = "",
       y = paste("Number of Contacts, N =", sum(nrow(d))),
       title = "Legislator Contacts with FERC") +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x.top = element_text())

all_contacts %>% 
  mutate(Type = as.character(Type)) %>% 
  filter(Type != "To be coded") %>%  
  mutate(total = n()) %>% 
  group_by(Type, total) %>% summarise(nT = n()) %>% 
  mutate(percent = paste0(nT, " = ", 100*round(nT/total, 2), "%")) %>% 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_col(aes(x = Type, y = nT)) + 
  geom_text(aes(x = Type, y = nT, label = percent), vjust = -.1) +
  labs(x = "",
       y = paste("Number of Contacts, N =", sum(nrow(all_contacts))),
       title = "All Legislators Contacts with Federal Agencies") +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x.top = element_text())

Members

Senators vs. state population

d %>% 
  filter(chamber == "Senate") %>% 
    group_by(member_state, year, pop2010) %>% summarise(n = n()) %>%
    group_by(member_state, pop2010) %>% summarise(mean = mean(n)) %>% ungroup() %>% 
    ggplot() + 
    geom_point(aes(x = log(pop2010), y = mean), color = "light blue") + 
    geom_smooth(aes(x = log(pop2010), y = mean)) + 
  geom_text(aes(x = log(pop2010), y = mean, label = ifelse(mean > mean(mean)*1.75, member_state, "")), check_overlap = F, size = 2.5, hjust = 0) + theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Senator Requests per Year by State Population",
       x = "Log State Population",
       y = "Average Number of Requests per Year")

Chamber = "Senate"

d %>% 
  filter(chamber == Chamber) %>% 
  group_by(state, Type) %>% summarise(n = n()) %>%
# map_id creates the aesthetic mapping to the state name column
ggplot() + 
  # map points to the fifty_states shape data
  geom_map(aes(map_id = state, fill = n), map = fifty_states) + 
  expand_limits(x = fifty_states$long, y = fifty_states$lat) +
  coord_map() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "", y = "", title = paste("Total Number of Contacts from members of the", Chamber)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank())# + facet_grid(. ~ Type)

d %>%

  group_by(state, pop2010, Type) %>% summarise(n = n()) %>% ungroup() %>%

        panel.background = element_blank()) #+

Interesting cases

In an article titled “Republican congressmen’s funding dwarfs challengers’”, the Charleston Gazee-Mail noted how energy companies backed Representative Alex Mooney (R-WV). Indeed, Mooney wrote to FERC more than any other agency, always on behalf of energy projects, mostly pipelines. In 2017, he wrote on behalf of the Dominion Energy Supply Header Project, National Fuel Gas Distribution Corporation’s Northern Access Project, Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company’s Atlantic Sunrise Project, Columbia Gas Transmission’s proposed Eastern Panhandle Expansion project, Columbia’s WB Xpress Project to build new compressor stations, In 2015 he wrote on behalf of the Columbia s Mountaineer XPress Project, Atlantic Coast Pipeline ACP project. The parent companies of these projects spend millions of dollars on lobbying (Lobbyview). The WV Gazette reports funding from Dominion that is not included in Lobbyview totals.

Committee Chairs

Chamber = "Senate"
dcommittees %>%  
  mutate(position = ifelse(position == "Other", NA, position)) %>% 
  filter(chamber == Chamber, 
         chair_since_2007 == T,  
         DATE < as.Date("2017-01-01"),
        DATE > as.Date("2007-01-01"),
        assigneddate < as.Date("2017-01-01"),
        terminationdate > as.Date("2007-01-01")) %>%
  select(DATE, chair, position, department, assigneddate, terminationdate, chamber, committee) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = DATE, 
        y = chair),
    shape = 73,
    size=2 
  ) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = chair, yend = chair, 
                   x = assigneddate, xend = terminationdate, 
                   linetype = factor(position)),
               position = position_nudge(y = -0.3)) +
  labs(title = paste(Chamber, "Committee Chairs"),
       y = "", 
       x = "" ) +
  scale_y_discrete(position = "right") +
  theme(
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 180, size = 5),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size=5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0)
  ) + 
  facet_grid(committee ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "both")

Many letters to FERC are cosigned

#A rough under-estimate based on whether "et al" or "&" appears in the summary:

FERC_letters %>% 
  group_by(ID) %>% 
  top_n(1) %>% 
  mutate(probably_cosigned = ifelse(str_detect(SUBJECT, "et al"), "et al",
                                 ifelse(str_detect(SUBJECT, "&"), "&", " neither"))) %>%
  group_by(year, probably_cosigned) %>% 
  tally %>% 
  ggplot() + 
  aes(x = year, y = n, fill = probably_cosigned) +
  geom_col()

Identified cosigned letters of those coded so far:

FERC_letters %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Freelancer)) %>% 
  mutate(cosigned = ifelse(!is.na(Cosigned_House)|!is.na(Cosigned_Senate),
                                 T, F)) %>%
  group_by(year, cosigned) %>% 
  tally %>% 
  ggplot() + 
  aes(x = year, y = n, fill = cosigned) +
  geom_col()

Companies

Top companies in pro-business letters

# Split out to one obs per member per letter per business
dcorps <- d %>%
  mutate(ProBusiness = ProBusiness %>% str_split(";")) %>%
  unnest(ProBusiness)

dcorps %<>% mutate(ProBusiness = ProBusiness %>%
                     str_replace("RTO", 
                                 "Regional Transmission Organization") %>%  
         str_remove_all(" Company.*| \\(.*| Inc.*| LLC.*| Energy.*") )%>%
  mutate(AntiBusiness = AntiBusiness %>% 
           str_replace("RTO", 
                       "Regional Transmission Organization") %>%  
         str_remove_all(" Company.*| \\(.*| Inc.*| LLC.*| Energy.*") )

dcorps %>%
  filter(!is.na(ProBusiness),
         !str_detect(ProBusiness, "Regional Transmission Organization") ) %>%
  group_by(ProBusiness) %>%
  select(id, last_name, ProBusiness, ID) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  summarise( n = n() , 
             members = str_c(last_name, collapse = "; "),
             ID = str_c(unique(ID), collapse = "; ")) %>%
  filter(n>quantile(n,.9))%>%
  arrange(-n) %>%
  knitr::kable()

Letters citing companies registered with FERC

Of the companies registered to interact with FERC, several appear in the letter texts. Here company_short is a shortened version a name that refrences several affiliated companies, each of which are registered separatly. TO DO: - (1) Identify linked corporations for other top companies in the data - (2) extract company contact persons and information from the FERC website.

load(here("data", "DOE_FERC-corps.Rdata"))
FERC_corps %<>% ungroup() %>% group_by(company_short) %>% mutate(industry = str_c(unique(industry), collapse = ";")) %>% select(-company, -Fortune500) %>% distinct() 

## Make a single string of short corp names
ferc_short <- unique(FERC_corps$company_short) %>% 
  str_c(collapse = "|") %>% 
  str_remove_all("||")

Company lookup table

Clean companies names extracted from letters and create shortened name that is more likely to be found in other datasets (like done with FERC-registerd companies above).

# Split out to one obs per member per letter per business
dcorps <- d %>%
  select(ID, bioname, ProBusiness, AntiBusiness, ProProject, AntiProject) %>% 
  gather(value = "company", key = "position", -ID, -bioname) %>%
  mutate(company = company %>% str_split(";")) %>%
  unnest(company) %>% distinct()

dcorps %<>% mutate(company = company %>%
                     str_replace("RTO", 
                                 "Regional Transmission Organization") %>%  
         str_remove_all(" Company.*| \\(.*| Inc.*| LLC.*| Energy.*") )

dcorps$company %<>%
  trimws()  # trim white space before and after company names

dcorps %<>%   filter(nchar(company)>1) %>%# drop names less than 1 character
  distinct() # drop duplicates

## For matching, remove endings like ", Inc." etc. 
trim <- function(d){
d %>%
  str_remove_all("Village of |\\(.*|,.*| -.*|^Proposed | Pipe.*| pipe.*| project$| Proiects$| Company.*| Comnany| Corp.*| Co$| Co.$| Energy$| energy$| power$| Power marketing$| Holdings.*| Group$| Gas$| Project.*| LLC| L.L.C.|  L.P.|^The | Inc.| L.P.| Ltd.| LP| Limited Partnership| Limited Liability|  Facility| Transportation and Storage| Storage and Transportation") %>% 
  str_remove_all("^, ") %>%
  trimws()  # filter out names less than 2 characters 
}



dcorps$company_short <- trim(dcorps$company) %>% trim()

    mutate(company_short = ifelse(str_detect(company, regex("Columbia Gas", ignore_case = T)), "Columbia Gas", company_short))%>%
  mutate(company_short = ifelse(str_detect(company, regex("Algonquin", ignore_case = T)), "Algonquin", company_short))%>%
    mutate(company_short = ifelse(str_detect(company, regex("Spectra", ignore_case = T)), "Spectra", company_short))%>%
  mutate(company_short = ifelse(str_detect(company, regex("Jordan Cove", ignore_case = T)), "Jordan Cove", company_short))%>%
    mutate(company_short = ifelse(str_detect(company, regex("Enron", ignore_case = T)), "Enron", company_short))%>%
     mutate(company_short = ifelse(str_detect(company, regex("Nexus", ignore_case = T)), "Nexus", company_short))%>%

  mutate(company_short = ifelse(company == "Express Pipeline", "Express Pipeline", company_short))%>%
  mutate(company_short = ifelse(company %in% c("American Energy", "American energy"), "American Energy", company_short))%>%
  mutate(company_short = ifelse(company_short == "AI", "AI Energy", company_short)) %>% 
  mutate(company_short = ifelse(company_short %in% c("N/A","Na","NO",
                                                     "Clean Water Act","Na",
                                                     "Energy", "West", "NA",
                                                     "Central", "Power", "Natural",
                                                     "Consumers"),
         "NOT A COMPANY?",  company_short))

Short company names, e.g. “Duke” may refer to many affiliated companies. The variable company_short_refs lists these affiliated companies.

#FIXME
# ADD company_short_refs 
dcorps %<>% 
  group_by(company_short) %>% 
  mutate(company_short_refs = str_c(unique(company), collapse = "; ")) %>% ungroup()

Look for problems with incorrect or over-trimed company names. For example what should we do with companies that are just state or city names? (e.g. El Paso Corporation, Tennessee Gas, American Energy, etc.)

## Inspect over-trimmed company names
dcorps %>% filter(company_short %in% c("", "NA", "na", "Na", "LLC", "Energy", "Pipeline", "Natural", "North", "New", "Express", "gas", "American", "Electric", "System", "Direct", "DC", "PS", "CT", "Forest", "International", "Tennessee", "Salt Lake", "Lakeside", "NW", "Jackson", "Public Service", "Peak", "Independence", "Select", "Portland", "Michigan", "Boundary", "Coastal", "Minnesota", "Midwest", "Northeast", "Columbia", "Plains", "Stream", "Mitchell", "AP", "Southern", "Ohio River", "Northwest", "Rio Grande", "AI", "Transportation", "12/20/2018", "Salem", "Boston", "Spokane", "El Paso", "Houston", "North American", "Consumers", "Advanced", "Complete", "Inland", "Limited Partnership", "RTO")) %>% select(company_short, company_short_refs, ID) %>% 
  group_by(company_short) %>%
  summarise(company_short_refs = str_c(unique(company_short_refs), collapse = "; "),
            IDs = str_c(unique(ID), collapse = "; ")) %>%
  distinct() %>% knitr::kable()

  group_by(company_short) %>%

Contributions from the Energy Sector

Using CRP industry codes for PACs and DIME contribution matrix, sum up sector-level contributions by memeber per year.

load(here("data/contrib_total.rds"))
contrib_total %<>% 
  rename(icpsryear = ICPSR,
         PAC_contributions = value)

d %<>% 
  # rounding years up is approximate, rewrite to go Nov-Nov?
  mutate(cycle = 2 * round(year/2) ) %>% 
  mutate(icpsryear = str_c(icpsr, cycle)) 

letters_money <- d %>% 
  filter(!is.na(ProBusiness)|!is.na(ProProject))%>% 
  group_by(icpsryear, cycle, name_state) %>%
  summarise(ProBusiness_Letters = n() ) %>% 
  # join by ICPSR, adding a sum of sector PAC contributions per member
  left_join(contrib_total) %>% ungroup()

letters_money %>% top_n(10, PAC_contributions) %>% knitr::kable()

Linear model: Pro-Business Letters per cycle ~ Energy Sector PAC contributions per cycle 2000-2016

lm(ProBusiness_Letters ~ PAC_contributions, data = letters_money) %>%
  tidy() %>% knitr::kable()
